WHAT WE DO

### Management consulting for growing businesses.

Fixed-scope consulting and advisory programmes for owner-led and professionally managed businesses. Senior-led — the people you meet are the people who do the work. Based in Bengaluru, working across India.

- 02

##### Plan

Reset, 30 days. Root cause found, fix designed.

- 03

##### Execute

Reset, 60 days. The same work, plus four weeks putting it in place.

- 04

##### Advise

Monthly. A senior sounding board once it’s running.

Most clients move through in that order. You can stop at any point. Or a custom engagement — if what you need doesn’t fit this sequence, we scope it with you before we begin.

HOW THE MONEY WORKS

#### One scope. One agreed fee.

Every programme is fixed-fee, agreed in writing before we start. No hourly billing, no scope creep, no surprise invoice at the end.

If you stop after the Diagnostic, that’s the whole engagement — no further obligation, no upsell conversation.

WHAT WE DON’T DO

- Run your finance, procurement, or operations team day to day. We build the system and train the people who run it

- Produce decks. You get short written documents your team can actually use

- Send a junior to do the work after a senior attends the first meeting. The people you meet are the people who do the work

- Sell you software you don’t need. The fix comes first; a tool only if it earns its place

- Take on work outside our expertise. If we can’t serve the problem well, we tell you upfront — and point you to someone who can

COMMON QUESTIONS

#### Fees and duration.

##### What is your consulting fee?

Every programme is fixed-fee, scoped to your situation and agreed in writing before we start. There is no hourly billing. Get in touch and we’ll share the fee for the programme that fits after a first conversation.

##### How long does a consulting engagement typically last?

The Diagnostic takes half a day. The Reset runs 30 or 60 days with weekly on-site visits. Ongoing Advisory is monthly, with a three-month minimum, for as long as it stays useful. Custom engagements have an end date agreed upfront.

##### Which programme should I start with?

Most clients start with the Diagnostic. If you already know the problem and have tried to fix it, the Reset is usually the right place. If you don’t need a project — just a senior sounding board — start with Ongoing Advisory. Not sure? Talk to us and we’ll tell you honestly.

##### How is payment structured?

Payment terms are fixed and agreed before the work begins — no open-ended billing, no surprise invoice at the end. We’ll walk you through them when we scope the engagement.

##### Can the engagement be done remotely?

Partly. The Diagnostic and Ongoing Advisory work well online. The Reset is built on weekly on-site visits, because operating problems are fixed where the work happens, not on a call. Outside Bengaluru, we agree the on-site rhythm with you before we start.

##### Who will actually do the work?

We do, personally. NXT Foundry is senior-led, not staffed out. You won’t be handed to a junior consultant after the first meeting.

##### What size of business do you work with?

Owner-led and professionally managed businesses, typically in the ₹50 Cr – ₹1,000 Cr revenue range. If you sit outside that, tell us — we’ll say honestly whether we’re the right fit.

##### Will you sign an NDA?

Yes. We’re happy to sign your NDA before the first detailed conversation, or share ours. What you tell us stays with us.

##### Do you offer business mentoring?

Yes — that is what Ongoing Advisory is. A senior thinking partner for founders and leadership teams, on call for the decisions that matter, without a project attached.

## [Our Approach](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#approach)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#approach

OUR APPROACH

### The recommendation is the easy part. The fix is the work.

We work inside the business — on the floor, with the finance team, in the warehouse — until the fix is in place and your people are running it. Senior-led, from the first conversation to the last review.

THE GAP

#### Most advice stops at the recommendation.

Growing businesses don’t lack advice. Auditors tell you what went wrong last year. Software vendors tell you their product will fix it. Large firms send a team, produce a report, and leave.

What’s harder to find is someone who stays for the unglamorous part — tracing the leak to its source, redesigning the approval that keeps failing, sitting with the team until the new way of working becomes the normal one.

That gap is where most operating problems survive. It’s the gap we were built to close.

SOUND FAMILIAR?

##### The signs we usually hear about first.

- Revenue is growing, but nobody can say with confidence what was earned versus what was actually received

- Month-end takes longer every quarter, and the numbers still get argued over

- Purchases, discounts, and credit notes get approved by whoever happens to be available

- Stock on the system doesn’t match stock on the floor, and margin drifts without a clear reason

- The same problem has been “fixed” twice already — and it’s back

“The hardest stretch isn’t starting up. It’s the one where the business has outgrown the owner’s memory, but the systems to replace it haven’t been built yet.”

— How we think about the work

THE PROCESS

#### Four steps. One team throughout.

01

#### Introductory call

A conversation about the business, the problem, and whether we are the right people for it. No pitch. If we’re not the right fit, we say so on the call — and point you to someone who is.

02

#### Diagnostic

A structured working session on the one problem you name. We trace it to the actual constraint — process, control, data, or ownership — not the symptom that brought you to us.

03

#### Fix, on site

Weekly visits to the floor, the finance team, the warehouse — wherever the problem lives. The fix is designed with the people who will run it, then put in place alongside them.

04

#### Review and hand over

We track outcomes, not activity. A weekly review rhythm is installed, owned by your team, and still running after we leave. That’s the test.

What the Diagnostic actually covers

- Where the money actually leaks — revenue, deductions, purchasing, stock, or all four

- Which controls exist on paper and which ones actually operate

- Who owns what, and where accountability quietly falls between two people

- The one change that, if made first, makes everything after it easier

HOW WE WORK WITH YOU

#### Structured for outcomes, not hours.

Scope

##### Agreed first

A written problem, scope, and end point before any work starts. If the scope needs to change, we agree that in writing too.

Cadence

##### Weekly, on site

Regular enough to keep momentum. Spaced so your team has time to do the work between visits.

Fees

##### Fixed, never hourly

One agreed fee per engagement. No hourly billing, no scope creep, no surprise invoice at the end.

Independence

##### Vendor-neutral

We don’t resell software. If a tool helps, we say so; if a spreadsheet and a discipline will do, we say that instead.

Location

##### Bengaluru-first

In person wherever the problem allows. Online works well for diagnostics and ongoing advisory across India.

Capacity

##### A few clients at a time

Depth needs focus. We take on a small number of engagements at once, and we’ll tell you when we’re full.

WORTH BEING DIRECT

#### We’re not the right fit for everyone.

If any of these describe you, we’ll probably say so in the first call — and save us both the time.

- Businesses looking for a report to justify a decision that has already been made

- Owners who want us to run a function permanently rather than build one that runs without us

- Teams unwilling to do the implementation work between visits — we work alongside you, not instead of you

- Pre-revenue or idea-stage startups — an accelerator will serve that stage far better than we can

OUTCOMES

#### What’s different when we leave.

Not frameworks in a slide deck. Working systems inside the business.

01

##### Clarity on the real constraint

Most businesses are solving the wrong problem. After the Diagnostic, you know exactly where the constraint is — and what to do about it first.

02

##### Revenue you can reconcile

What was earned, what was received, and why they differ — visible every month, not reconstructed at year-end.

03

##### Controls that actually operate

Approvals, limits, and checks that work in practice — not a policy document nobody has opened since it was written.

04

##### An operating rhythm that holds

A weekly review your team runs without being chased. Numbers that are current, decisions that are recorded.

05

##### Decisions tested before they’re made

A senior second opinion on the calls that matter — a price change, a vendor switch, a new channel, a senior hire.

06

##### Documentation your team owns

Short, plain-language process notes and checklists. Written for the people who use them, not for a filing cabinet.

READY TO TALK?

No pitch, no proposal on the first call. Just a direct conversation about the problem and whether we can help.

## [Cutting €42 million of unmapped purchase orders to €12.3 million](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/automotive-po-invoice-lifecycle)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/automotive-po-invoice-lifecycle

All stories

AutomotiveTech implementation

EW Procure to PayFinancial ControlsIT Operations

### Cutting €42 million of unmapped purchase orders to €12.3 million

#### 01 · The problem

A large automotive organisation’s IT operations involved multiple service areas, including Data Centre, Network, SAP, Workplace, Information Security and Service Desk.

€42M sitting in unmapped purchase orders across IT service areas

Purchase order and invoice information was distributed across SAP exports, Excel files and stakeholder-maintained trackers. Finance, procurement and delivery teams lacked a consolidated view of the PO lifecycle, making it difficult to identify unmapped purchase orders, reconcile invoices and resolve outstanding exceptions. This resulted in:

- Significant value sitting in unmapped purchase orders

- Manual reconciliation across fragmented data sources

- Delays in identifying invoice and service-confirmation mismatches

- Limited ownership and visibility of outstanding financial exceptions

#### 02 · Where the value sat

Unmapped purchase-order value

Before

€42M

After

€12.3M

−70.7% as teams worked through the exceptions the dashboard surfaced.

The PO lifecycle, and where exceptions hid

- 01PO created and approvedUnmapped POs

- 02Service confirmationUnlinked confirmations

- 03InvoicingMulti-service contractsInvoice mismatches

- 04PaymentPartial payments

One view across every stage, with long-pending values aged by service area — Data Centre, Network, SAP, Workplace, Information Security and Service Desk.

#### 03 · What we did

We developed a Power BI-based PO and invoice lifecycle dashboard to bring together information from finance, procurement and delivery teams. The solution included:

- PO lifecycle tracking: consolidated visibility from PO creation and approval through service confirmation, invoicing and payment

- Exception management: identified unmapped POs, partial payments, multi-service contracts and unlinked service confirmations

- Financial reconciliation: compared PO values, invoiced amounts and payments to identify outstanding balances and discrepancies

- Aging analysis: highlighted long-pending and unresolved PO values across service areas

- Stakeholder-level reporting: enabled teams to filter and investigate exceptions by service line, region, PO value and status

- Governance and monitoring: supported recurring reviews with finance, procurement, delivery and PMO stakeholders

#### 04 · The outcome

−70.7% unmapped PO value, down from €42 million to €12.3 million

The dashboard improved financial visibility and helped teams systematically investigate and resolve outstanding PO mapping issues.

Unmapped PO value reduced from €42 million to €12.3 million, a reduction of approximately 70.7%.

The initiative also established a more structured approach to PO tracking, invoice reconciliation and cross-functional exception management.

Automotive · IT operations · Procure to pay

Client identity and confidential operational details have been withheld.

## [Closing ₹5 crore of revenue leakage in a fitness chain’s access controls](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/fitness-access-controls)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/fitness-access-controls

All stories

Fitness & wellnessConsulting project

EW Revenue LeakageAccess ControlsInternal Audit

### Closing ₹5 crore of revenue leakage in a fitness chain’s access controls

#### 01 · The problem

A leading fitness and wellness chain had a streamlined membership and access model, but weaknesses in its operational controls were creating opportunities for revenue leakage. Our audit identified three key vulnerabilities.

₹5 Cr in revenue leakage exposure across access and operational control gaps

Membership access misuse. Members were accessing multiple centres simultaneously using QR codes, fingerprints and multiple devices. Attendance records showed impossible concurrent entries across geographically distant locations. Our investigation identified approximately ₹2 crore in potential revenue leakage associated with such access misuse.

Unauthorised group-class access. Certain centre managers were booking classes under their own credentials for unauthorised attendees. In some instances, unofficial trainers were also using gym facilities to offer paid training independently.

Manual gate access misuse. Centre managers could operate swing barriers using separate remotes intended for housekeeping access. These were sometimes misused to admit non-members outside the standard membership process, particularly at franchise-operated centres.

#### 02 · Where people got in

Revenue leakage exposure found by the audit

₹2 Cr₹3 Cr

- Membership access misuse ₹2 Cr

- Other access and operational gaps ₹3 Cr

≈ ₹5 crore in overall exposure across the access and operational control gaps.

Three ways in, outside the membership process

- App and biometric entry

GapOne membership on several devices, with impossible concurrent entries across distant centres.

FixOne registered device and one sign-in method; changes need a CX request and approval.

- Group classes

GapManagers booked classes on their own logins for unauthorised attendees; unofficial trainers ran paid sessions.

FixNew KPIs on access exceptions, so each centre’s unusual activity is visible and accountable.

- Swing barriers

GapHousekeeping remotes opened gates for non-members, mostly at franchise centres.

FixGate openings and closures monitored and matched against an actual entry or exit.

#### 03 · What we did

We conducted a revenue and access-control audit, working with the IT and revenue teams to assess vulnerabilities and strengthen controls across the membership journey.

Device-level access controls. Membership access was restricted to one registered device. Device changes required a Customer Experience (CX) request and approval. Repeated changes triggered temporary restrictions and further investigation.

Single-mode authentication. Members could access facilities through either QR authentication or fingerprint verification. Switching the access method required a CX ticket and appropriate approval.

Gate-level accountability. Swing-barrier operations were brought under monitoring, tracking gate openings, closures and whether an actual entry or exit occurred.

Operational monitoring. Additional KPIs were introduced to improve visibility into access exceptions and strengthen centre-level accountability.

#### 04 · The outcome

1 device per membership, with any change approved through Customer Experience

The audit identified approximately ₹5 crore in overall revenue leakage exposure across the access and operational control gaps, including approximately ₹2 crore associated with membership access misuse.

The resulting control improvements strengthened membership authentication, reduced opportunities for unauthorised access and improved accountability over physical entry points.

Fitness and wellness · Multi-centre chain

Client identity and operational details have been withheld for confidentiality.

## [Bringing accountability to a ₹76 crore warehouse reconciliation gap](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/warehouse-stock-transfers)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/warehouse-stock-transfers

All stories

E-commerceTech implementation

EW Warehouse OperationsSupply ChainInventory Controls

### Bringing accountability to a ₹76 crore warehouse reconciliation gap

#### 01 · The problem

A large e-commerce business was struggling to reconcile stock transfers between its warehouses. Dispatching warehouses recorded the quantities sent, while receiving warehouses sometimes recorded different SKUs and quantities. Despite these mismatches, transfer orders were frequently closed based on expected quantities and email confirmations rather than verified receipts.

₹76 Cr of stock dispatched between warehouses in six months, with no verified receipt

An audit of six months of stock transfers identified approximately ₹76 crore worth of inventory dispatched under STOs for which the business no longer had clear visibility of the final receipt or whereabouts. The underlying process also exposed the business to estimated quarterly inventory losses equivalent to approximately 17% of transferred material value.

The root cause was disconnected warehouse systems and a reconciliation process that largely depended on month-end reviews.

#### 02 · Where it broke

Follow one stock transfer

Where it brokeWhat we put in place

##### 1 · Warehouse A dispatches

Records the SKUs and quantities sent under a stock transfer order.

##### 2 · Warehouse B receives — different SKUs, different count

Nobody is told to expect it, so mismatches aren’t caught at the dock.

Fix Advance notice to the receiving warehouse, with transfer-specific SKU IDs and shelf-life data.

##### 3 · Transfer closed on an email

Closed on the expected quantity, not the verified receipt.

Fix A four-hour reconciliation window after receipt; unresolved gaps escalate automatically.

##### 4 · Found at month-end — if at all

By then, stock and accountability are hard to trace.

Fix Open transfers stay visible in each warehouse’s performance tracking.

#### 03 · What we did

We supported the development of a separate reconciliation tool that brought greater accountability and visibility to inter-warehouse stock movements.

The solution introduced advance notifications to receiving warehouses, followed by a four-hour reconciliation window after receipt. Unresolved discrepancies triggered automated escalations to warehouse managers and operations leadership, while open transfers remained visible in warehouse performance tracking.

We also introduced transfer-specific SKU identification to strengthen audit traceability and incorporated remaining shelf-life information for perishable inventory, helping receiving warehouses prioritise older stock for fulfilment.

#### 04 · The outcome

~5% of monthly stock transfers still open in disputes, after the fix

The proportion of monthly stock transfers remaining open due to disputes between warehouses reduced to approximately 5%. The intervention significantly reduced inventory losses and improved the visibility, traceability and accountability of stock movements across warehouse locations.

E-commerce · Warehouse Operations · Bengaluru, India

Client identity and engagement details are withheld for confidentiality.

## [Breaking the cycle of slow and non-moving inventory in B2B wholesale](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/wholesale-slow-moving-inventory)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/wholesale-slow-moving-inventory

All stories

E-commerceConsulting project

EW Inventory HealthProcurement ControlsDemand Planning

### Breaking the cycle of slow and non-moving inventory in B2B wholesale

#### 01 · The problem

A large B2B wholesale e-commerce business was experiencing a growing accumulation of slow and non-moving (SNM) inventory across multiple categories and warehouses.

30–40% forecast accuracy, driving manual overrides and excess buying

Despite having inventory provisioning policies and demand-planning processes, aged inventory continued to accumulate while fresh purchase orders were being raised. Financial provisioning was taking place, but the underlying stock was not being cleared. The assessment highlighted four interconnected challenges:

- Inventory accumulation: significant working capital remained locked in inventory aged beyond 180 days

- Weak procurement controls: Open-to-Buy (OTB), SKU run-rate limits and unhealthy-item restrictions were not consistently enforced

- Forecasting gaps: forecast accuracy remained around 30–40%, increasing reliance on manual overrides and contributing to excess procurement

- Regional inventory imbalance: stock remained idle in low-demand locations while other regions experienced shortages, with no systematic trigger for redistribution

#### 02 · The broken loop

Demand, buying and stock weren’t talking to each other

- Forecast

GapAround 30–40% accurate, so planners overrode it by hand.

FixSeasonal and regional recalibration, MAPE tracking, overrides only for defined exceptions.

- Purchase order

GapOTB, run-rate and unhealthy-item limits weren’t consistently enforced.

FixAutomated checks, PO restrictions, classification approvals and escalation of breaches.

- Inventory

GapStock idled in low-demand regions and aged past 180 days — provisioned, but not cleared.

FixRedistribution before reordering, and a Power BI view of ageing and liquidation.

ASP–MSP–PO variance monitoring feeds what was actually bought back into the next plan.

#### 03 · What we did

We assessed the inventory planning, procurement and replenishment processes and identified opportunities to strengthen the feedback loop between demand, buying and inventory execution. The proposed improvements covered six areas:

- Inter-warehouse redistribution: SKU-level inventory ageing and sales-velocity comparisons to identify stock that could be transferred from low-demand to high-demand regions before placing fresh orders

- Forecasting improvements: recalibrating forecasting models using seasonal and regional demand signals, introducing MAPE as a performance measure and restricting manual overrides to defined exceptions

- Purchase-order controls: stronger OTB, SKU run-rate and unhealthy-list controls through automated checks, PO restrictions and escalation of significant policy breaches

- Provisioning and liquidation visibility: a Power BI dashboard to track provisioned inventory, ageing and liquidation opportunities, helping teams distinguish financial provisioning from actual stock clearance

- Inventory classification governance: stronger controls over A/B/C/D/O inventory classification, including approval requirements and purchase restrictions for selected inventory categories

- Sales-plan and procurement alignment: an ASP–MSP–PO variance monitoring approach to identify deviations between sales plans and actual purchasing decisions

#### 04 · Intended impact

6 fixes across forecasting, buying, redistribution and stock visibility

The interventions were designed to improve inventory health and working-capital efficiency by:

- Reducing avoidable procurement of slow-moving inventory

- Improving stock availability through regional redistribution

- Strengthening compliance with purchasing policies

- Improving visibility into inventory ageing and liquidation requirements

- Establishing clearer accountability for forecast deviations and procurement decisions

B2B wholesale e-commerce · Inventory and procurement

Client identity and confidential engagement details have been withheld. Specific improvement opportunities and control mechanisms are described at a high level.

## [Automating 94 payroll checks for apparel manufacturers](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/payroll-compliance-framework)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/payroll-compliance-framework

All stories

Apparel manufacturingConcept

Payroll ControlsAutomationInternal Audit

### Automating 94 payroll checks for apparel manufacturers

#### 01 · The problem

Apparel manufacturing businesses often manage complex payroll processes involving large workforces, multiple salary components, attendance records and statutory deductions. Manual verification across these areas can create significant operational effort and increase the risk of errors, missed exceptions and delayed payroll processing.

90+ manual checks before every payroll run, with verification taking up to seven days

The conceptual assessment identified several common challenges:

- More than 90 manual checks required before payroll processing

- Significant HR and payroll manpower involved in routine validation

- Verification cycles extending up to seven days

- Risk of errors in sensitive employee, banking and salary data

- Limited visibility into payroll exceptions and control effectiveness

#### 02 · The control map

94 checks across eight control areas

01Employee status

Joining and exit dates, status, employee ID

02Banking details

Bank account and IFSC changes, duplicate accounts

03Payroll processing

PAN and Aadhaar changes, salary variances, overtime, leave adjustments

04Headcount

Month-on-month and department-level comparisons

05Payroll components

Basic pay, DA, allowances, deductions, bonuses

06Leave and attendance

Leave balances, absences, leave encashment

07Tax and statutory

TDS, PF, ESI, tax exemptions

08Internal audit controls

Duplicate payments, data integrity, change monitoring, exceptions

Every area is checked before disbursement, on one dashboard for HR, Finance and Internal Audit.

Payroll verification time (illustrative)

Manual

7 days

Automated

2 days

5 days sooner in the illustrative scenario — not a verified client result.

#### 03 · What we did

We developed a conceptual Power BI-based payroll compliance framework using Power Query and DAX to automate 94 payroll validation and internal audit checks, structured across eight control areas:

- Employee status: joining and exit dates, employee status and employee ID validation

- Banking details: bank account and IFSC changes, duplicate account identification

- Payroll processing: PAN and Aadhaar changes, salary variances, overtime and leave adjustments

- Headcount: month-on-month and department-level workforce comparisons

- Payroll components: basic pay, DA, allowances, deductions and bonuses

- Leave and attendance: leave balances, absences and leave encashment

- Tax and statutory compliance: TDS, PF, ESI and tax exemption validation

- Internal audit controls: duplicate payments, data integrity, change monitoring and exception reporting

The dashboard was designed to help HR, Finance and Internal Audit teams identify discrepancies before payroll disbursement.

#### 04 · Illustrative impact

7 → 2 days illustrative payroll verification time with the checks automated

The framework demonstrates the potential to:

- Reduce payroll verification time from seven days to two days

- Automate the review of 94 recurring checks

- Improve visibility into exceptions and payroll control performance

- Reduce repetitive manual validation and free up HR resources for higher-value activities

- Strengthen audit readiness through structured exception reporting

Apparel manufacturing · Payroll

This is an independently developed conceptual framework. All examples, figures and business scenarios are illustrative and are not presented as verified client implementation results.

## [Choosing where to build: a what-if framework for 17 cities](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/global-location-strategy)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/global-location-strategy

All stories

Banking & financial servicesConcept

Location StrategyDecision SupportPower BI

### Choosing where to build: a what-if framework for 17 cities

#### 01 · The problem

Organisations evaluating new operational or innovation centres across multiple countries must balance cost, talent availability, regulatory requirements and geopolitical risks.

17 cities, including five Indian metros, compared on five strategic dimensions

Comparing locations using disconnected reports and inconsistent data makes it difficult for leadership teams to assess trade-offs and establish a consistent basis for decision-making. The conceptual framework evaluated 17 global cities, including five major Indian metropolitan cities, across five strategic dimensions:

- Cost attractiveness

- Data storage and security

- Political and regulatory environment

- Talent availability

- Geopolitical stability

#### 02 · What we did

We developed an interactive Power BI city evaluation dashboard to consolidate multi-source research into a consistent, comparable decision-support framework. The solution included:

- Standardised city scoring: normalised different quantitative and qualitative indicators onto a common 0–10 scoring scale

- City comparison scorecards: side-by-side assessment of cities across all five strategic dimensions

- Global and India views: switch between the international shortlist and Indian city comparisons

- Interactive ranking and heatmaps: relative strengths and weaknesses across the 17 locations

- What-if scenario analysis: select two evaluation criteria and dynamically reposition cities on an interactive scatter plot

- Strategic fit matrix: cities grouped into a 3×3 matrix to highlight strong candidates and locations involving significant trade-offs

#### 03 · Try the what-if

The most useful part isn’t the scorecard — it’s the what-if view. A leadership team can change its priorities and see how the relative attractiveness of cities shifts. Try cost vs talent, data security vs cost, or geopolitical stability vs talent.

Across (x)Up (y)

Indian metroGlobal cityIllustrative data: anonymised locations and scores, not real city ratings.Best fit for this pairing

- IN-1Indian metro · 8.6 + 8.8

- IN-2Indian metro · 8.9 + 8.1

- IN-3Indian metro · 9.1 + 7.4

5 of 17 land in the top-right cell, strong on both criteria.

Change either criterion and the shortlist moves with it — that’s the trade-off made visible.

#### 04 · Strategic value

10 what-if pairings of the five criteria, from cost vs talent to security vs cost

The framework was designed to help leadership teams:

- Compare global expansion locations using a consistent evaluation methodology

- Understand trade-offs between cost, talent, security and geopolitical considerations

- Test different strategic priorities through interactive scenario analysis

- Shortlist locations for deeper feasibility assessments and business-case development

- Communicate location-selection rationale through a common visual framework

Location strategy · 17 cities · 5 dimensions

This is an independently developed conceptual framework. The cities, scoring methodology and examples are illustrative and do not represent an actual banking institution’s expansion decisions.

## [Spotting counterfeit risk on a marketplace before customers do](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/marketplace-anti-counterfeit)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/#stories/marketplace-anti-counterfeit

All stories

E-commerceConcept

Brand ProtectionRisk AnalyticsMarketplace Trust

### Spotting counterfeit risk on a marketplace before customers do

#### 01 · The problem

Large e-commerce marketplaces operate across extensive seller networks, product categories and constantly changing listings. Traditional rule-based monitoring and reactive customer complaints can make it difficult to identify suspicious sellers and potentially counterfeit products before they affect customers.

5 risk areas, from listing manipulation to seller re-entry

The conceptual assessment identified several risk areas:

- Listing manipulation: frequent changes to product descriptions, MRP and listing attributes could help suspicious sellers evade conventional monitoring

- Seller re-entry: previously delisted sellers could attempt to return through alternate accounts, devices or addresses

- Unusual pricing behaviour: abnormal MRP fluctuations and discount patterns could indicate deceptive pricing or suspicious listing activity

- Returns and complaint anomalies: unusually high return rates, negative feedback and counterfeit complaints could signal potentially problematic products or sellers

- Fragmented risk intelligence: seller, listing, transaction, customer feedback and device data were not being considered together in a unified risk assessment

#### 02 · How a risk is scored

Many signals, one score, a clear next step

SignalsMRP and price changesDiscount patternsListing editsRatings and reviewsReturn ratesCounterfeit complaintsSeller historyDevice and address signals

- LowKeep monitoring

- MediumWatch closely; re-score as signals change

- HighAlert and manual investigation — not automatic removal

Verified investigation outcomes feed back into the models, so detection improves over time.

#### 03 · What we did

We designed a conceptual anti-counterfeit intelligence framework combining listing-level monitoring, seller behaviour analysis and risk-based investigation. It covered four capabilities:

- Listing risk identification: monitored listing quality, MRP changes, pricing volatility, customer ratings and return patterns to identify suspicious product listings

- Seller behaviour intelligence: compared active seller profiles against previously flagged seller patterns using pricing behaviour, category activity, complaint history, addresses and device-level signals

- Composite risk scoring: combined multiple risk indicators into a structured scoring model to classify listings and sellers into low-, medium- and high-risk categories

- Investigation and feedback: a workflow for risk alerts, manual investigation, enforcement actions and feeding verified outcomes back into the detection framework

The proposed architecture combined:

- SQL-based data extraction and integration

- Python-based anomaly detection using techniques such as Isolation Forest and DBSCAN

- Similarity analysis to identify seller behaviour patterns

- Time-series analysis of pricing and MRP movements

- NLP-based customer review and sentiment analysis

- Power BI dashboards for risk monitoring, exception tracking and investigation prioritisation

Three things set it apart:

- Behavioural seller matching: going beyond individual listing checks to identify patterns associated with previously flagged sellers

- Multi-signal risk scoring: combining pricing, returns, complaints, listing quality and seller history rather than relying on one indicator

- Closed-loop risk management: feeding verified investigation outcomes back into the detection models to improve future identification

#### 04 · Intended impact

3 tiers of risk — low, medium and high — each with its own review route

The framework was designed to help marketplaces:

- Identify suspicious listings and sellers earlier

- Prioritise investigations based on risk severity

- Detect repeat offenders and potential seller re-entry

- Improve visibility into counterfeit-related returns and complaints

- Support regulatory compliance monitoring

- Strengthen marketplace trust and brand protection through proactive monitoring

A suspicious price movement or a high return rate is a risk signal, not proof that a product is counterfeit. The framework is built to prioritise human review, not to replace it.

E-commerce marketplace · Brand protection

This is an independently developed conceptual framework. The models, thresholds, expected improvements and examples are illustrative and are not verified implementation results.

## [FAQ](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/faq.html)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/faq.html

### Frequently asked questions

Fees, duration and how we work. If your question isn’t here, email hello@nxtfoundry.in.

#### What is your consulting fee?

Every programme is fixed-fee, scoped to your situation and agreed in writing before we start. There is no hourly billing. Get in touch and we’ll share the fee for the programme that fits after a first conversation.

#### How long does a consulting engagement typically last?

The Diagnostic takes half a day. The Reset runs 30 or 60 days with weekly on-site visits. Ongoing Advisory is monthly, with a three-month minimum, for as long as it stays useful. Custom engagements have an end date agreed upfront.

#### Which programme should I start with?

Most clients start with the Diagnostic. If you already know the problem and have tried to fix it, the Reset is usually the right place. If you don’t need a project — just a senior sounding board — start with Ongoing Advisory. Not sure? Talk to us and we’ll tell you honestly.

#### How is payment structured?

Payment terms are fixed and agreed before the work begins — no open-ended billing, no surprise invoice at the end. We’ll walk you through them when we scope the engagement.

#### Can the engagement be done remotely?

Partly. The Diagnostic and Ongoing Advisory work well online. The Reset is built on weekly on-site visits, because operating problems are fixed where the work happens, not on a call. Outside Bengaluru, we agree the on-site rhythm with you before we start.

#### Who will actually do the work?

We do, personally. NXT Foundry is senior-led, not staffed out. You won’t be handed to a junior consultant after the first meeting.

#### What size of business do you work with?

Owner-led and professionally managed businesses, typically in the ₹50 Cr – ₹1,000 Cr revenue range. If you sit outside that, tell us — we’ll say honestly whether we’re the right fit.

#### Will you sign an NDA?

Yes. We’re happy to sign your NDA before the first detailed conversation, or share ours. What you tell us stays with us.

#### Do you offer business mentoring?

Yes — that is what Ongoing Advisory is. A senior thinking partner for founders and leadership teams, on call for the decisions that matter, without a project attached.

Still deciding? Start with a conversation.

## [Privacy Policy](https://www.nxtfoundry.in/privacy.html)

URL: https://www.nxtfoundry.in/privacy.html

### Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026

This policy explains what information NXT Foundry collects through www.nxtfoundry.in, why we collect it, who processes it for us, and how to contact us about it. NXT Foundry is based in Bengaluru, India. Questions about this policy go to hello@nxtfoundry.in.

#### Summary

- When you send an enquiry, we collect the details you type into the contact form and use them only to respond to you.

- We do not sell your information or use it for advertising.

- The website uses Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights, which do not set cookies. Google Analytics sets cookies only if you accept them in the cookie banner. Otherwise it records visits without cookies.

- Files you open in the Vendor Payable Reconciliation tool are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to us.

- We do not currently use any AI service to process information from this website.

#### 1. The contact form

##### What you give us

Field | Required? |

Name | Yes |

Business email | Yes |

Phone number (with country code) | No |

Company | Yes |

Business type | No |

Area of interest | No |

Message | Yes |

##### What is added automatically

- A submission reference and timestamp, so a retried submission is not stored twice and we can refer to your enquiry.

- A hashed version of your IP address. Your IP address is converted into a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA-256) on our server. The raw IP address is not stored, logged or passed on. The hash is used only to limit how many enquiries can be sent from one connection in a short time.

- A hashed version of your email address (SHA-256), used only to limit repeated submissions from the same address.

- How long the form took to fill in, and a hidden field that people never see. Both are basic checks against automated spam.

##### Why we use it

To read and reply to your enquiry, to follow up on the conversation you started, and to protect the form from spam and abuse. We do not add you to a mailing list.

##### Where it goes

- The form sends your details to our server, hosted on Vercel.

- From there, the details are stored in a Google Sheet in NXT Foundry's Google Workspace account, through Google Apps Script.

- An email notification with your enquiry is sent to our inbox (hello@nxtfoundry.in) through Gmail.

Our server logs record only whether a submission succeeded or failed. They do not contain your form entries or your IP address.

##### How long we keep it

We have not set a fixed deletion schedule. We keep enquiries while they are useful for the conversation they started. You can ask us to delete yours at any time (see section 6).

#### 2. The reconciliation tool

The Vendor Payable Reconciliation tool opens with sample data. Ledger files (CSV or Excel), PDFs and other documents you open in the tool are read and processed in your browser. They are not uploaded to NXT Foundry or sent to any other service, and they are not kept after you close or reload the page.

Features marked ✦ in the tool are previews of AI features that are not switched on. They do not send any data. If we switch them on, we will update this policy first.

#### 3. Analytics and cookies

##### Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights

We use Vercel Web Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights to understand which pages are visited and how fast they load. These tools do not use cookies. They collect information such as the page visited, the referring site, browser and device type, operating system, approximate country, and page-load performance. We use this information only in aggregate.

##### Google Analytics

The website loads Google Tag Manager, which runs Google Analytics 4, on every visit. It uses Google's Consent Mode, so how it works depends on your choice in the cookie banner.

- If you click “Not now” or ignore the banner, Google Analytics sets no cookies. It still sends Google a basic, cookieless record of your visit, such as the page viewed, the time, your browser and device type, and your approximate location derived from your IP address. Without a cookie, it cannot recognise you on later visits. Google may use these records to estimate overall visitor numbers.

- If you click “Let’s do it”, Google Analytics also sets first-party cookies (named _ga and _ga_<ID>) that let it recognise repeat visits from the same browser and see how visitors move between pages.

Advertising and ad-personalisation settings are always off. We use the reports to understand how the website is used and to improve it.

##### Cookies and browser storage we use

Name | Type | Set by | Purpose | Lasts |

_ga | Cookie | Google Analytics | Distinguishes one browser from another, so repeat visits can be counted. Set only after “Let’s do it”. | Up to 2 years |

_ga_<ID> | Cookie | Google Analytics | Keeps track of the current visit (session). Set only after “Let’s do it”. | Up to 2 years |

nxt-analytics-consent | Local storage | This website | Remembers your choice in the cookie banner, so we don’t ask on every visit. | Until you clear it |

nxt-tour-*, nxt-recon-collapsed-* | Local storage | This website | Remember whether you have seen a tool’s guided tour and which panels you collapsed. | Until you clear it |

nxt-interest | Session storage | This website | Carries the products you picked on the Products page into the contact form. Removed once it is used. | Until the tab is closed |

Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights do not use cookies or browser storage.

##### How to control cookies

- On this website. Use the Cookie settings link at the bottom of every page of the main website to change your choice at any time. If you choose “Not now” after accepting, the Google Analytics cookies are deleted straight away.

- In your browser. Every major browser lets you block or delete cookies, either for all websites or only for www.nxtfoundry.in:

- Chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Third-party cookies / Site settings → Cookies and site data

- Edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions → Manage and delete cookies and site data

- Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data

- Safari (Mac): Settings → Privacy → Manage Website Data; Safari (iPhone/iPad): Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data

Clearing “site data” for www.nxtfoundry.in also removes the local storage items listed above, including your banner choice, so the banner will appear again.

- Block Google Analytics completely. Google offers the Google Analytics Opt-out Browser Add-on, which stops Google Analytics on every website, including the cookieless visit records described above. Many content and tracking blockers do the same.

- Private browsing. In a private or incognito window, cookies and browser storage are deleted when you close the window.

Blocking cookies or browser storage does not stop the website or the contact form from working.

#### 4. Other services and storage in your browser

- Hosting. The website is hosted on Vercel. Like any web host, Vercel receives technical information, such as your IP address and browser details, when your browser requests a page.

- Fonts. The website loads its typeface from Google Fonts, so your browser connects to Google's servers, which receive your IP address and browser details.

- Browser storage. Apart from the Google Analytics cookies described above, which are set only with your consent, we do not set cookies. The website keeps your cookie-banner choice and a few small settings in your browser's local storage or session storage, such as whether you have seen a tool's guided tour, which summary panels you have collapsed, and the products you picked on the Products page so they can be filled into the contact form. These stay on your device, and you can clear them through your browser settings.

#### 5. Who we share information with

We share information only with the service providers named above, and only so they can provide their services to us: Vercel (hosting and analytics) and Google (Google Workspace, Gmail, Google Fonts and Google Analytics). These providers may process data on servers outside India. We do not sell personal information. We may disclose information if the law requires us to.

#### 6. Your choices and contacting us

You can write to hello@nxtfoundry.in to:

- ask what information we hold about you from an enquiry,

- ask us to correct it, or

- ask us to delete it.

It helps to include your enquiry reference (it starts with “NXT-”) if you have it. You can also contact us by email instead of using the contact form.

#### 7. Changes to this policy

If we change how we handle information, for example by moving enquiries to a different system, we will update this page and the date at the top.
